items.title: What Changed In Dell's Story?
items.summary: Dell Technologies' (DELL) management no longer leads its earnings calls with the topic it stressed two years ago. That topic has not disappeared. Management still talks about it. The business behind it still brought in $51.0 billion, about 45% of Dell's revenue, in fiscal 2026. So it matters to you. What did Dell's management use to lead with.

items.title: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (HPE) Brings Quantum Computing Into On Premises HPC
items.summary: Hewlett Packard Enterprise (NYSE:HPE) said it will integrate QuEra Computing's fault-tolerant quantum systems with its Cray supercomputers for on premises HPC environments. The collaboration targets national labs, enterprises and high performance computing centers that want quantum and classical workloads on a single infrastructure. items.title: Is SanDisk Stock Amplifying A Risk You Already Own?
items.summary: SanDisk (SNDK) has run up 23.3% over the last five trading days, while the S&P 500 added 2.4%. A move like that in a NAND maker pulls money in. But next week's price is not the question. What matters is what owning the stock does to your money when the market moves, because SanDisk travels much further than the index in both directions.

items.title: Cisco Stock Looks Expensive Until You Price The Year It Already Guided
items.summary: Cisco Systems (CSCO) trades near $106 a share, about 24.6 times the $4.33 of non-GAAP earnings per share it reported for fiscal 2026. That is the same basis Cisco uses for its guidance and analysts use for their forecasts. For a networking supplier with $63.33 billion of revenue behind it, that is rich. And it ignores the two years analysts have already forecast.
